text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein gets telephone call from Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat briefing him on latest consultations with Israel and U.S.-Palestinian talks.
- Royal palace announces the engagement of Princess Rahma, the Crown Prince's daughter, to Al'aa Batayneh in a family ceremony attended by King Hussein.
- German firm undertakes studies to privatise the water sector in the Amman municipality.

- Prime Minister Kabariti meets a delegation of farmers from the Jordan Valley and says agriculture is a "strategic, security and political issue": PM questions the indebtness of farmers and says the intention is to set up a large marketing company to help farmers export their produce.
- Parliament to begin debating the 1997 fiscal budget on Tuesday by discussing the financial committee's report on the budget.
- Head of the computer department in the land registry department sent to court on misuse of authority by awarding computer tender to his own private company.
- Lebanese authorities remove administrative measures barring exports of Jordanian agricultural produce.
- The government will adjust bread prices lower in the next two weeks after the drop in grain prices, a ministry of supply source says.

- Justice Minister says there are 300 detained people in the second batch of prisoners who are qualified for release under the royal pardon granted to hundreds arrested in the aftermath of civil disturbances last August.
- Efforts under way to convince Minister of Communications Sarayrah to withdraw his resignation from the cabinet but efforts appear deadlocked, sources say.
